title: Starting with one server
idea: A one-server setup runs your app and its database on a single machine. It is the simplest design, and a sound place to start.
points: One machine runs the app, the database and local files.
It is simple: one thing to deploy, and database calls stay on the machine.
The app and the database compete for the same CPU, memory and disk.
One failure or restart takes the app and the database down together.

hero.title: What the two share on one machine
head: Shared resource

hero.caption: Which limit you reach first depends on your workload. Measure before you change anything.

pitfalls: Measure CPU, memory and disk first; do not guess which limit you hit.
Keep the database port closed to the internet; only your app needs it.
Back up the database to another place; one disk is a single copy.

quiz.q: Your app and database run on one server. The machine fails. What happens?
options: Only the app stops; the database keeps serving
Both stop until the machine returns
Traffic moves to a second server
The database keeps serving cached reads
quiz.why: Both share one machine, so one failure stops both. Spare servers and copies come later, and you add them on purpose.

takeaway: Everything on one server shares its limits and fails together.
